summary: Standing aside holds up. The Proposer made no proposals and I can only approve or shrink, so the trade list was empty. The reasoning was sound on the information available: cash was 11.6% with a thin buffer, any buy that kept a 10% cushion would have been about $9 (token-sized, ruled out by L4), and the market note was neutral with AI-capex, hawkish-Fed and Binance stress. The close agrees with the call. Equity ended at 603.07 (day -2.18, drawdown 0.94%) while SPY fell about 1.4% on the day (agent +0.51% since start vs SPY -1.40%), and invested return is +0.62%. The cost of the cautious posture is visible but modest: the account is 88.3% invested against 99% for the shadow portfolio, which is up 4.8%, so idling about 12% in cash has lagged the benchmark book. That gap comes from the earlier ramp-in (invested 53% on 10-21), not from today. Skeptic's point stands: the weak spot was held-position review, not the missing buy. Of the three items I raised, none has changed the verdict. IDXX fell 4.3% today (position -0.8% on cost, 6.6% of equity) with its print on Mon 11-02; I held through it and that now carries live event risk, which I accepted knowingly (about $3 stress loss). BTC is -8.2% on cost, about 2% above its invalidation level. DPZ's invalidation is still stale. Net: no decision looks wrong, but three held-position items need action next session.
lessons: L1 (still open, 8th session): DPZ's $274.88 invalidation sits about 13% below the $316.58 fill. Nothing is broken (DPZ -0.9%), but the level cannot trigger meaningfully. I flagged it again today without fixing it, because the PM only writes decision and review files. The next decision run should state the re-anchored level (about $285) in its reasoning and the orchestrator or Reviewer should write it into the DPZ thesis.

BTC/USD thesis is close to its stop: the invalidation is a close more than 10% below the $83,686 fill (about $75.3k). BTC is about $76.8k (-8.2%), so it is about 2% from the trigger, and the other invalidation clause (an exchange failure) is arguably brushing against the record Binance hack. I judged it contained (BTC fell only about 3%), but the next PM should check Binance withdrawal or solvency news first and sell the whole position if the $75.3k close occurs, with no discretionary hold.

IDXX print on Mon 11-02 is the main single-position event risk (6.6% of equity, down 4.3% today, two PT cuts). Its invalidation is a close below $500.22 or a 5-point underperformance of XLV over 21 days. The rule for next time: when a held name has a high-risk print one trading day out and the thesis was written before that date was known to be inside the window, say explicitly why holding is acceptable, as the Skeptic asked. I did, with the stress-loss figure, but the thesis itself still says earnings are outside the 5-day window, which is now stale.

CARG has a company-confirmed print on 11-05 after the close, 4 trading days out. Its thesis said earnings were outside the 5-day window and invalidates on a negative surprise inside 5 days. Position is 5.1% of equity and +2.5%. This is the next event to review if sizing is ever revisited, not an action now.

A no-trade day should still carry a held-position review (invalidation distance to current price, event dates inside the window, thesis text that has gone stale), since that is where the Skeptic's valid objection landed. Make that review a standing part of the decision reasoning rather than waiting for the Skeptic to raise it.
